name: TVS Motor Company Ltd.
business_summary: India's third-largest two-wheeler maker and a leading three-wheeler/EV player (iQube, Orbiter, King EV Max), with Norton Motorcycles and Swiss E-Mobility Group assets. Motorcycles/scooters ~80% of revenue, exports ~28% of volumes, and a consumer-finance arm (TVS Credit) being demerged. Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): record revenue Rs 17,103 cr (+39% y/y per FPJ; +44% per ET), profit up 46-52% (Rs 1,219-1,377 cr depending on perimeter), EBITDA +47%; record market share. October 2026 two-wheeler sales +22% to 5.15 lakh units; total +29%. Market cap ~Rs 2.1 lakh cr; stock +28.7% in 12 months. Screener dossier unavailable.

revenue_mix.segment: Financial services (TVS Credit), to be demerged

new_nodes_proposed.name: Competitive intensity in Indian two-wheelers/EV two-wheelers

exposures.mechanism: Domestic 2W/3W ~70% of volumes. +10% industry volumes => TVS revenue +7%; incremental margin ~25% vs ~12.5% EBITDA margin (estimate; Q2 EBITDA +47% y/y per NDTV Profit) => EBITDA +14%; EV/MCap ~1.05; persistence 0.5 => ~+7. October 2W sales +22% to 5.15 lakh show momentum.

Aluminium (engine, wheels, castings) ~8% of costs => 7% of revenue; +10% => 0.7% of revenue; at 12.5% margin => EBITDA -5.6%; 40% passed through => -3.4%; x1.05 x0.3 => -1.1. Empirical -1.48 (t=-2.0) agrees. Aluminium is -19.6% since June, a current tailwind.
Steel ~15% of costs => 13% of revenue; +7% => 0.9% of revenue => EBITDA -7.4%; 60% unrecovered => -4.4%; x1.05 x0.3 => -1.4.
Copper in wiring/motors (higher for EVs) ~2.5% of costs; fundamental effect is small (-0.3), but empirical -1.19 (t=-2.0) per +10% suggests extra cyclical co-movement; blended -0.5.
Tyres ~6% of costs; rubber ~35% of tyre cost; +10% rubber => tyre +3.5% => 0.18% of revenue => EBITDA -1.4% x1.05x0.3 => -0.3 (partly passed through).
Petrol cost and petrochemical inputs (~5% of costs) weigh on commuter demand and margins; exports to oil-exporting economies partly offset. Empirical -0.44 (t=-1.0).

Exports ~28% of volumes (Africa, LatAm, ASEAN, Middle East; USD pricing) vs imports ~10% of revenue (EV components, Norton, SEMG): net long ~18% of revenue; +3% => +0.54% of revenue; 70% flow-through (hedging) => EBITDA +3%; x1.05 x0.5 => +1.6.

evidence.note: NDTV Profit preview: strong volumes, exports

exposures.mechanism: High-beta (1.5) quality compounder with premium multiple: significant empirical -1.55 (t=-3.1) per +25bp. US 10-year at 4.89%, +9.4% since June.

~70% of 2W retail is financed (entry segment more price/EMI sensitive); +25bp => volumes -0.6% => EBITDA -1.2%; plus TVS Credit funding margin until demerger; x1.05x0.5-0.6 => -1.0. RBI hiked to 5.50% on 7 Oct.

evidence.note: CNBC TV18: auto stocks fell on hike

exposures.mechanism: Empirical DXY -1.91 (t=-2.3) per +3% is a flow channel: a stronger dollar means FPI outflows from high-beta Indian discretionary stocks. +US$5bn quarterly inflow => +2.5.

EVs (iQube, Orbiter, e-3W) ~8-10% of volumes; EV capacity rising to 80,000 units/month (Business Upturn 2026-10-28). +1 stronger push => EV share +3pp => revenue +1-2%, margin accretion small initially; incentive-linked => +3.

China rare-earth magnet tightening constrains e-scooter motor supply; Q1 analyst calls flagged an EV capacity crunch (NDTV Profit 2026-08-10). +1 => EV output -15% (~1.5% of group volume) plus premium lost => EBITDA -3% x1.05x0.5 => ~-2.

Pricing/market-share war with Honda, Hero, Bajaj and EV start-ups (Ather, Ola). +1 => -1pp share (~-5% volume) or -1% price => EBITDA -10% x1.05x0.25 => -2.5. TVS currently gaining ('record market share', NDTV Profit).
Premium 125cc+ motorcycles (Apache, Ronin, Raider), Jupiter 125, Norton, EVs lift ASP and margin. +1 => +1.5% ASP drop-through => EBITDA +10% x1.05 x0.25 => +2.5.
Exports ~28% of volumes; Africa+LatAm ~40% of exports => ~11% of volume. +1pp regional growth with export elasticity ~2 => +0.2% group revenue => EBITDA +0.5-1% => +1.
ASEAN, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal exports ~10% of volumes; +1pp growth => +0.8.
